title: The Wettest Jump
lines: It was the hottest day of the summer.
Meg and Tim sat on the back steps.
The steps got too hot to sit on.
"I am so hot," said Tim.
Dad said, "Get your hats. We can go to the pool."
The water in the pool was cold and blue.
"My splash is bigger," said Tim.
"No, mine is the biggest," said Meg.
Tim ran and jumped in with a yell.
His splash was small. It got no one wet.
Meg jumped next, but hers was smaller still.
They jumped and jumped for a long time.
Both kids got wetter and wetter.
But no splash was big at all.
Then Meg sat on the step and had a plan.
"Dad," she said, "you must jump with us."
Dad set down his book and got up.
All three went in at the same time.
That was the biggest splash of the day.
Water went up over the wall of the pool.
Meg and Tim were the wettest kids there.
"That was better than winning," said Meg.
They went home wet and happy.

questions.ask: What were Meg and Tim trying to do?
questions.listenFor: Make the bigger splash, then the biggest splash. Have them read the two quotes.

questions.ask: Whose plan was it for Dad to jump too?
questions.listenFor: Meg's. The line before the quote says she had a plan.

questions.ask: Do you think Meg and Tim minded getting wet? Why?
questions.listenFor: Either answer. The hot day in the first line is a good reason to point at.
